_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

**Should this draft publish as written, get a hard revise, or stay draft until something concrete changes?**

### White / First Principles

Known: draft is `draft: true`, ~180 lines, hero is still `image-template.jpg`. It documents a real sequence—full archive council (DNPAP, Facebook Favorites), then one-agent hats on notes features, then a frame correction when “AI powers this” was underplayed. The skill `six-hats` already exists and cites this draft as method source. Structure: problem → council sting → de Bono table → map → why five agents → loop → notes case study → steal-the-refusal close.

Unknown / checkable: whether readers can follow Color / Advisor naming without the skill; whether DNPAP/Facebook details match what you actually did to those posts; whether the notes-features “second run” is verifiable or reconstructed memory; word count and voice lint status. Assumption to strip: “cousin of Karpathy + de Bono” is enough reason for a stranger to finish. Stake is publish trust for a meta-AI-workflow post, not a ranking tip URL.

### Red / Instinct

Proud of the sting-and-correction arc. Tired of the middle third—tables and loop numbers feel like skill docs leaking into a blog. Ending lands. Title’s clever; the body sometimes teaches the skill instead of telling the night.

### Black / Contrarian

This post has a fatal shape risk: **method manual with memoir garnish.** The council stories earn their keep. The notes garden run earns its keep—especially the “half-wrong / reframed / opinions moved” beat. Between them sits a long stretch that re-explains Six Hats, remaps five advisors, and pastes the loop almost as the skill already states it. A reader who never opens Cursor gets homework they won’t run.

Second failure mode: **unearned authority.** You assert the cheap loop “proved” itself because Chairman sounded adult then corrected. That’s one author’s self-report, not evidence independence was preserved. You admit Expansionist smells Contrarian in one window, then claim process fixes it—without showing a failed soft-merge example in the prose.

Third: **anti-slop blockers.** `image-template.jpg` blocks ship. The Color / Advisor labeling and “no applause track” refrain risk sounding like product copy for your own skill. The map table is honest but dense; it asks the reader to care about your Cursor taxonomy. If the post is “I don’t want yes-men,” the middle third is a yes-man to the repo.

### Yellow / Expansionist

If it works, this becomes the portable piece of your AI writing system: not “use five agents,” but **refuse the single soft answer.** The DNPAP sting + Facebook ten-minute Executor + notes frame-flip is a rare honest demo that cheap friction still catches category errors. People who burned tokens on multi-agent theater will feel seen. The close (“Don’t ask whether your idea is good—wear Black until it finds something”) is quotable and teachable without Cursor.

Upside chain: post → skill discovery for readers who already use agents → clearer mental model for when to pay for real independence. The half-wrong Chairman story is the differentiator—most AI workflow posts only show the pretty verdict. You show the frame was wrong and the hats had to re-run. That’s the product.

### Green / Options

1. **Publish after cut:** Keep open + council sting + notes case + close. Collapse hat table + advisor map + full numbered loop into a short “what I run” paragraph + link/mention that the skill lives in the repo. Ship when hero image exists.
2. **Do nothing / stay draft:** Fine until you’ve actually demoted DNPAP/Facebook or documented the IA split—then the post has receipts, not just transcripts.
3. **Split:** Short opinion post (“cheap friction vs war room”) now; separate “how the loop works” note or skill README later—don’t make the blog the skill body.

### Outsider

A stranger sees: guy invents a meeting format for chatting with ChatGPT, names colors after a famous book, maps them to his Cursor plugins, then says the expensive version stung him about a song page and a Facebook tip. The notes part is long product navel-gazing (OKF, Duo, shareable grids) with jargon outsiders won’t decode. Weirdest claim: that labeled paragraphs in one chat are meaningfully different from “just ask the model to be critical.” Without a side-by-side of soft vs forced output, it reads like branding. Also weird: teaching a full procedure in a personal essay.

### Executor

Monday step: cut or fold sections “Six hats I already knew,” “Five advisors, mapped,” and the full numbered loop into ≤120 words of “what the cheap loop is,” then replace `image-template.jpg` or leave `draft: true`. Don’t publish until that cut is done.

### Self-review

1. **Strongest block:** Black—the “method manual with memoir garnish” diagnosis names the real publish risk.
2. **Biggest blind spot:** Whether voice already passes jorap-voice / lint; this run didn’t score the prose.
3. **What all blocks missed:** Audience fork—Cursor users vs general “AI workflow” readers—and whether related_notes / tags overpromise a digital-garden tutorial.

### Blue / Chairman

## Where the lenses agree
The open, council stings, and notes reframing are the post. The middle teaching block is the liability. Don’t ship with a template hero. The close already has the take.

## Where the lenses clash
Yellow wants the method visible so people can steal it; Black/Outsider say the full loop+map is skill leakage that kills strangers. Green’s “do nothing until receipts” fights Yellow’s “this is already a good portable idea.”

## Blind spots
No voice/slop score in this pass. No check that DNPAP/Facebook status on the live site matches the narrative. Insider jargon density in the notes section.

## The recommendation
**Hard revise, then publish—not ship as written, not idle forever.** Keep the lived arc (council sting → cheap hats → wrong frame → corrected IA split → steal the refusal). Cut the encyclopedic middle: one short “what I mean by hats vs council” beat, not three sections of tables and a nine-step paste. Prove the post is an essay about refusing yes-men, with the skill as a footnote, not the other way around. Then fix the hero image and clear draft.

## The one thing to do first
Rewrite so “What I actually ran” jumps nearly straight to “First real hats run” after a **tight** hats-vs-council paragraph (no full map table, no numbered loop dump)—park the procedure in the skill.
